standard: 232.0-B-4 Cor. 1 — Frame Delimiting and Fill Removal
provenance_note: 232.0-B-4 prints no example frame or CLCW. Hand-derived from 232.0-B-4 with Cor. 1: §4.1.2 (Primary Header bits 0-1 TFVN 00, 2 Bypass, 3 Control Command, 4-5 spare, 6-15 SCID, 16-21 VCID, 22-31 Frame Length = total - 1, 32-39 N(S); Table 4-1, flags 0/1 reserved), §4.1.3 (Segment Header: Sequence Flags 2 bits, Table 4-2, MAP ID 6 bits; Unlock = 00, Set V(R) = 82 00 V(R)), §4.1.4 (FECF: CRC with G(X) = X^16 + X^12 + X^5 + 1, register preset to ones), §4.2.1 (CLCW fields and widths), §4.4.9.2-3 (delimiting and validation), §4.4.3.3 and §4.4.7.3 (invalid MAP and VC), §5 and §6.3, §6.6 (managed parameters, Security Header after the Segment Header). Check order, validation reason codes, the delimiter's valid header, and the managed parameters kept, as docs/standards/tc-frame.md states them. SCID 0x155 is the fictional SCID of the reference scenario (APP-026). Expected values computed by an independent Python model of those clauses, written before the Rust codec, which shares no code or method with it (the header is one 40-bit integer, the CRC is bitwise from G(X)). Error cases name the field code of 03 §9.1. The BC Unlock frame of tc-bc-unlock-enc-001 and the CLCW of tc-clcw-enc-001 are worked by hand, the CRC register octet by octet, in docs/verification/derivations/tc-frame.md. The model is committed as test-vectors/models/tc_frame.py (TV-023); `python3 -I test-vectors/models/tc_frame.py --check test-vectors/tc/*.json` recomputes every expected value. Author of the model: an AI agent, Claude Opus 5.5, recorded as co-author of commit afff003 (2026-10-23), whose message states that it wrote the model from 232.0-B-4 Cor. 1 before the Rust codec existed; the history records no briefing of the agent beyond that statement (TV-023). This file covers Frame Delimiting and Fill Removal.

cases.description: One frame filling the data unit exactly
Two frames and three octets of fill 0x55 (fewer than a header)

Three frames and six octets of fill 0x55: TFVN 01 is not a valid header (§4.4.9.2.6 note 2). The rest is reported as Fill, which is the reading of OI-41 item 2; the Blue Book only requires the octets to be discarded
A frame, then a frame cut short: the rest is discarded as a truncated frame (§4.4.9.2.5)
An empty data unit yields nothing
A header that declares a 5-octet frame is not a valid header: fill (OI-41 item 2, a project reading)
Frames without FECF back to back, then four octets of zero fill
Five zero octets of fill: TFVN 00, but a Frame Length of 1 octet
